original_question_en: How many edge colors are necessary if every four-vertex clique must contain at least five colors?
answer: The Erdős-Gyarfas function f(n,4,5) equals 5n/6 + o(n) (Banerjee-Bradshaw-Letzter-Pokrovskiy, arXiv:2207.02920).
statement: f(n,4,5) = 5n/6 + o(n), i.e. for every eps > 0 and all large n, |EG n - 5n/6| <= eps*n, where EG n is the least number of colours in an edge colouring of K_n in which every K_4 spans at least five colours (JSP140.FiveSixth JSP140.EG, JSP140.jsp_000140_target).
notes: Round 10: build OK, 0 sorry/admit, partial_ok=true, missing_theorems=[jsp_000140_main]. ROUND 10 PROVES THE COMPLETE LOWER HALF OF THE HEADLINE, with the sharp constant 5/6 and no o(n) loss. NEW FILE lean/JSPProblem/Cherry.lean (zero sorry), which discharges the single hypothesis that round 4 had isolated for the whole BCDP22 lower bound (Paths c <= n(n-1)/6, i.e. at most n^2/6 two-edge paths, equivalently: at least two thirds of all edges lie in single-edge components of their colour class). (1) cherry_four_ne - THE K4 CONSTRAINT THROUGH A TWO-EDGE PATH: if a - v - b is a two-edge path of colour i and x is a fourth vertex, then the other four edges s(a,b), s(a,x), s(b,x), s(v,x) of the K4 carry FOUR PAIRWISE DISTINCT COLOURS, none of them i (the K4 carries i twice, must span five colours, and may not carry i a third time). (2) centre_eq_of_leaves / centre_eq_of_leaves' - A PAIR OF LEAVES DETERMINES THE CENTRE: two two-edge paths with the same two leaves coincide. (3) nb_eq_singleton_of_cherry - THE EDGE BETWEEN THE LEAVES IS AN ISOLATED SINGLE EDGE: with j = c s(a,b) one has j != i, nb c j a = {b} and nb c j b = {a}. (4) not_two_centres, leaf_not_centre. (5) cherryEdges / card_cherryEdges / cherryEdges_disjoint - THE COUNTING: the two edges of a two-edge path together with the single edge between its leaves form a three-element set of edges, and the sets belonging to DIFFERENT two-edge paths are PAIRWISE DISJOINT (four cases: two path edges -> not_two_centres; path edge vs leaf edge -> a path edge is never single and a leaf edge always is; two leaf edges -> centre_eq_of_leaves'). (6) Cherry.three_mul_paths_le_edges - THE 5/6 COUNTING LEMMA: 3 * Paths c <= |E(K_n)| = n(n-1)/2, hence Paths c <= n(n-1)/6, unconditionally (six_mul_paths_le, paths_le). (7) Cherry.five_sixth_lower: every admissible k-colouring of K_n (n >= 4) uses at least 5(n-1)/6 colours (5(n-1) <= 6k); EG_ge_five_sixth, EG_ge_five_sixth_real. (8) Cherry.fiveSixthLower_eps: for every eps > 0 and all n >= max(ceil(5/(6 eps)), 4), 5n/6 - eps*n <= f(n,4,5). MAIN RESULTS in Main.lean: fiveSixthLower_eg : FiveSixthLower EG (THE LOWER HALF OF jsp_000140_main, complete) and admissibleLower_eps : AdmissibleLower 1 (the same in the Admissible-colouring language of jsp_000140_target_iff); fiveSixthShape_five_sixth (5n/6 - 5/6 <= f(n,4,5) <= 5n/6 + n/6 + 1 for all n >= 4, the lower side improving from n/12 + 3/4 to the sharp 5/6); fiveSixthShape_sixth_residue' (the SYMMETRIC bound |f - 5n/6| <= n/6 for n >= 5, n != 4 mod 6, which round 9 could not prove); fiveSixth_ge_sixth and fiveSixth_eps_ge_sixth: the catalogue estimate |f(n,4,5) - 5n/6| <= eps*n for EVERY eps >= 1/6 (on n != 4 mod 6), with the sharp constant on both sides (round 9: eps >= 1/4). The classical constant 3/4 of Erdos-Gyarfas (1977) is thereby replaced by the sharp 5/6 of BCDP22. STILL MISSING for jsp_000140_main: only the UPPER half for 0 < eps < 1/6, i.e. an admissible colouring of K_n with 5n/6 + o(n) colours - the BCDP22/JoMu22 construction (1-factorisations of hypergraph matchings); the available constructions are the sum colouring (n colours) and the ghost colouring (n-1 colours for n = 0,2 mod 6), both within O(n) of the target. The residual class n = 4 mod 6 still only has f <= n+1.
